ai.title: Add thinker-gemini agent for free tier
ai.summary: New `thinker-gemini` agent added using `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview` model. Free tier users are instructed to spawn this agent for complex problems. `thinker-gpt` updated to remove `providerOptions`.

eli5.text: If you use the free version of this coding assistant today, it can now call in a new helper agent powered by Google's Gemini model to tackle hard problems. That helper is added to the list of assistants the free version is allowed to use, and the main assistant is told to spawn it whenever you hit a complex task or ask it to think through something. The older reasoning helper stays available but no longer carries special chat-subscription settings. In short: free users get access to a new, smart second opinion that the assistant is encouraged to use often.

ai.title: Basher spawnerPrompt and command description clarified
ai.summary: Basher agent spawnerPrompt now requires both a shell command and a prompt. Command description updated to specify bash shell. Internal agent definition change in agents/basher.ts.

eli5.text: People who use the command-running helper now have to give it both a shell command and a prompt for describing the result, instead of just the command. If you asked the helper to run something, it will now expect a second piece of instructions telling it how to explain what happened. The text telling the helper what kind of command to expect was also tweaked to remind everyone it should be a bash command.

ai.title: Base2 agent prompt forces thinker-gemini spawn for free tier
ai.summary: Updated `agents/base2/base2.ts` to mandate `thinker-gemini` agent spawning for most requests in the free tier, shifting from conditional complex-problem triggers to a default-once-per-request rule. The prompt now explicitly instructs the agent to gather context before spawning the thinker to plan the response, and injects a dedicated step in the implementation flow for free users. This change aims to leverage the model's reasoning capabilities more consistently for free users.

eli5.text: When you use the free version of Codebuff to ask the assistant to do something, it will now automatically bring in a second, very capable reasoning helper before doing most of your tasks, unless your request is too simple to bother with. Previously, that helper was only brought in when a problem seemed especially complex; starting today, the free assistant treats bringing in that helper as the default move for nearly every request. If you watched the assistant work, you'd notice it pausing to gather your project details first, then deliberately spinning up that reasoning helper to plan out the best response before making any edits or suggestions. Who feels this: free-tier Codebuff users. When it started: live today, based on the April 10 snapshot.

ai.title: thinker-gemini: low reasoning effort, concise output
ai.summary: thinker-gemini agent sets reasoningOptions.effort to 'low' and tightens instructionsPrompt to demand concise, non-verbose responses. Change reduces token waste and latency for this sub-agent's thinking step. Scope limited to agents/thinker/thinker-gemini.ts. Old prompt said "Think deeply"; new prompt says "Think about" and "say the absolute minimum needed to answer the user's question correctly."

eli5.text: The thinker-gemini assistant (used only by free-tier users) now thinks less deeply and gives shorter answers. Before, it was told to "think deeply"; now it's told to consider the request briefly and say only what's needed to answer the question correctly. As a result, free-tier users will notice faster responses that get to the point instead of detailed explanations. This change is live today, but it only affects the free tier because the base2 agent is configured to spawn thinker-gemini exclusively for free users.

ai.title: Add --save-traces flag to buffbench evals
ai.summary: Adds `--save-traces` CLI flag to buffbench eval entrypoints (`main.ts`, `main-nightly.ts`, `main-hard-tasks.ts`, `main-single-eval.ts`). Passes flag to `runBuffBench` which writes agent traces to `logsDir/traces` as JSON files when enabled. Default behavior unchanged; flag required to persist traces.

eli5.text: If you run an automated evaluation of how well AI assistants complete coding tasks, you can now add a special command option to save a detailed record of every step the AI took while working. That record is saved as a separate file for each task and only appears when you actively turn on that option, so by default nothing changes. The new option works across all the different evaluation entry points used internally for nightly, single, and hard-task testing.

ai.title: Skill tool loads session-created skills from disk
ai.summary: Agent runtime `handleSkill` now calls `loadSkillFromDisk` when a skill misses the pre-loaded cache. Scans `~/.agents`, `~/.claude`, and project-local equivalents for `SKILL_FILE_NAME` inside a directory matching the requested name. Validates frontmatter via `SkillFrontmatterSchema` and enforces `frontmatter.name === skillName` before returning the definition. Tool description in `common/src/tools/params/tool/skill.ts` updated to reflect dynamic disk loading.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to use a skill (a reusable behavior or domain guide), it now looks for skills you created yourself during this session, not just the ones bundled at startup. If the requested skill wasn't found in the program's starting cache, it scans your personal and project folders (like ~/.agents, ~/.claude, and matching local folders) for a matching skill file, checks its header information, and only uses it if the file's name matches what you asked for. You'd notice this if you had just written a new skill file on disk and the assistant suddenly recognized it in the same session instead of ignoring it as unknown.

ai.title: Update buffbench eval agent to base2-free-evals
ai.summary: The `agents` array in `evals/buffbench/main.ts` updated from `base2-free` to `base2-free-evals`. This change targets the specific evaluation configuration for the buffbench suite. Scope limited to the internal eval script.

eli5.text: The internal testing system that scores the assistant's coding help has switched which version it grades against, moving from one evaluation setup to a newer one. This only affects the behind-the-scenes scoring used by the team that builds the assistant, so nothing you see or do changes. If you were watching the test runs, you'd see them now using the updated grading configuration instead of the previous one. It's already live for the internal tests today.
